mechanism: Load scheduled macro events from a CSV (country;GMT release;name) into an OO news container; for each event open a ±timeWindow (default 600s) listening gate and read iMomentum(Symbol, PERIOD_M1, 13, PRICE_CLOSE); treat momentumBuffer[0]>100.10 as upward impulse and <99.90 as downward impulse, advancing the news index after a decision.
data_needed: CSV news calendar with GMT release times; live M1 Momentum(13) on close; TimeGMT(); open-position guard.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Chart symbol (USD-news examples on FX); PERIOD_M1; dummy and DailyFX USD calendar July 2013.
why_new_for_mis: Gates a classical momentum reading to an event clock so MIS senses news-timed impulse vs quiet time, not a continuous oscillator alone.
quote: Checks momentum's turbulences around the time of the news release

mechanism: Reactive news EA: when the event-window momentum spikes up (>100.10) it sells expecting short-term retract; when momentum spikes down (<99.90) it buys expecting bounce—using the news-timed impulse as a volatility shock to fade rather than follow.
data_needed: Same news CSV + Momentum(13) M1; SL=400 / TP=600 points example; one position at a time.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: FX chart symbol; M1; USD macro releases.
why_new_for_mis: Frames post-news momentum extremes as a fadeable shock sensor (impulse→retrace) rather than a trend-follow breakout.
quote: when a strong upward movement occurs, the EA assumes that the price will retract and therefore sells. Similarly, when there is a strong downward movement the robot places a long position

mechanism: Build point-and-figure columns on log10(price) with optimizable box size (pips) and reverse count so instruments spanning cents to tens of thousands share one scale; X columns mark bullish box advances and O columns bearish—primary-trend regime from column type, with support/resistance and pivot levels stored per column.
data_needed: Tick/bar prices; box size; reverse; log-price PnF column array (max/min, resist/supp, column_type).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD example Box-20 Reverse-3; FX majors/crosses; Dow CFDs (#AA…#XOM, #SPY, #QQQ); box 10/20/50/100; multi-year history for large boxes.
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a noise-filtered, scale-free directional regime from log-PnF columns instead of time-based candles.
quote: I use the price logarithm for the point and figure chart to avoid setting values of one to tens of thousands of pips for the box size.

mechanism: Strategy 1 places buy-stops above prior X-column high when price is above support / sell-stops below prior O-column low below resistance, trailing SL at the PnF pivot (max/min ± reverse·box). Strategy 2 buys resistance-line break and sells support-line break with SL at pivot and trail on the trend line—break of geometric PnF levels as the change event.
data_needed: Live PnF column geometry (resist_price, supp_price, max/min_column_price, reverse, double_box); pending stop orders.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same FX + stock CFD sets; box 10–100; 2012–2013 optimization; risk per trade opt_f and max DD gate.
why_new_for_mis: Treats PnF geometric S/R and pivot distances as explicit breakout/change sensors with precommitted invalidation, not discretionary lines.
quote: buy when it breaks through the resistance line, sell when it breaks through the support line; set stop loss at the pivot level, set trailing stop at the trend line.

mechanism: Four-analyst discretionary stack: each runs technicals (mostly horizontal S/R; some chart/candlestick patterns), then correlates with economic news to estimate the usual daily range and only trades when risk/reward justifies (e.g. prefer Sell Limit at completed double-top vs chasing a 70-point bullish daily-range call).
data_needed: Intraday S/R levels; chart/candle patterns; economic calendar; subjective daily-range estimate; R:R filter.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD examples; intraday (not long-term trend focus); Forex generally.
why_new_for_mis: Casts expected daily range as a news-conditioned volatility budget that gates pattern entries—soft but explicit range sensor for MIS.
quote: We all do technical analysis, and then we correlate it with the economic news to estimate the usual daily range.

mechanism: Find the two nearest upper and two nearest lower iFractals on D1; map each D1 fractal day onto M15 and search the ~96 intraday bars for the true high/low (ArrayMaximum/Minimum on CopyHigh/CopyLow or iHigh/iLow arrays) so support/resistance trendline anchors have 15-minute time/price precision instead of D1 bar open time.
data_needed: D1 fractal buffers; M15 high/low/time for each fractal day; history-loaded check (iBarShift==-1 or Bars==0 alert).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GBPNZD examples; fractals PERIOD_D1 (1440); clarification PERIOD_M15; any Symbol().
why_new_for_mis: Cross-TF extreme refinement yields sharper S/R geometry than raw HTF fractal timestamps—useful structural sensor for MIS.
quote: you can't just draw the lines on a larger timeframe - the line should be plotted by extreme points with accuracy up to 15 minutes.

mechanism: Ray support/resistance OBJ_TREND through the two clarified lower (upper) fractal extrema; on H4, compare prior-bar close to ObjectGetValueByShift/ByTime at that bar—breakdown if Close<support, breakup if Close>resistance—with ≤1 push notification per 4 hours.
data_needed: TL_Support/TL_Resistance objects; H4 close and time; line price at that time; notification throttle.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Chart Symbol(); structure from D1/M15; breakthrough confirmed on PERIOD_H4.
why_new_for_mis: Separates HTF structure building (D1 fractals) from LTF break confirmation (H4 close), a clean multi-scale change sensor.
quote: The trend line is plotted through the extreme points of the day timeframe, but to identify the breakthrough earlier, the bar must be closed lower or higher than the trend line on H4.
